# Backtesting platform UI/UX design plan: addendum

Oct 7, 2026 · @qiwen

## Purpose

This addendum supplements Backtesting platform UI/UX design plan without changing its structure. It adds the four things the plan describes only in prose: how a researcher moves through the product step by step, what the key pages look like, how data flows inside the frontend, and how numbers and words are written on screen.

| Part | Adds | Supplements plan section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Key flows | Four core paths drawn and broken into steps | 3 Information architecture, 10 Interaction rules |
| B. Page wireframes | Composer, run analysis and trade card layouts | 4, 6 and 7 |
| C. Frontend architecture and data flow | Data layers, state ownership, loading and caching, performance budget, interaction feel, stack | 11 State design, 14 Backend contract |
| D. Content and formatting rules | Numbers, units, dates, ids, labels, microcopy | 12 Visual system |

Everything here follows the plan's principles: runs are immutable, the backend computes every number, realism assumptions are tested and never tuned, and the research protocol is built into the interface.

## A. Key flows

Four paths carry most of the daily work; each ends in something the researcher can keep or share, usually a comparison link. The diagram shows them at a glance and the tables give each step: where the user is, what they do, and what the screen does in return.

> **Diagram, page 2 of the source PDF** — *Key flows · 4 paths, 5 steps each*
>
> Not reproduced in this conversion; see `Plan/Backtesting platform UI UX design plan addendum.pdf`, page 2.

Each lane reads left to right; the tinted box is what the path leaves behind, usually a link someone else can open.

### Flow 1: change one slot and compare

The most frequent path. Target: 2 steps to submit, 1 click from the finished run to its comparison.

| # | Where | User does | Screen responds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Run analysis | Clicks "Edit and rerun" in the header, or a slot name anywhere on the page | Composer opens with this run's config as the baseline; the clicked slot's card is open |
| 2 | Composer | Swaps the variant or changes a parameter | A baseline dot appears on the field; the top line reads "Differs from baseline in 1 slot" |
| 3 | Composer (optional) | Runs a preview for a date | Candidate states and selected contracts for that date within 10 s |
| 4 | Composer | Presses Run (Cmd + Enter) | Job tray shows the run queued, then progress; the composer stays open for the next variation |
| 5 | Job tray | Clicks "Compare with baseline" on the finished toast | Comparison: config diff with the one slot highlighted, metrics with intervals, trade- level diff |
| 6 | Comparison | Labels the run "candidate" or "rejected", or opens its Robustness tab | Label shows in the log; the comparison URL is the shareable answer |

### Flow 2: explain a loss

From a dip on the equity curve to the component action behind it, without leaving the page.

| # | Where | User does | Screen responds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Overview tab | Drags across the drawdown on the underwater chart | Every layer zooms to the range; the trade table filters; a range chip appears in the top tier |
| 2 | Attribution tab | Switches tab (range kept) | Greeks waterfall and P&L by closing component for the range |
| 3 | Attribution tab | Clicks the largest bar, e.g. a slot or vega | Trade table filters to trades where that slot or Greek drove the loss, worst first |
| 4 | Trade table | Presses Enter on the first row | Trade card opens; the chart shades its holding period |
| 5 | Trade card | Reads the lifecycle timeline and clicks the closing action | Action log highlights the row with reason and triggering data values; context values at that moment |
| 6 | Trade card (optional) | Runs a counterfactual exit | Paired run created; result labeled in-sample, opened in comparison |

### Flow 3: from a promising run to paper trading

The gate every strategy passes before it touches the paper account.

| # | Where | User does | Screen responds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Robustness tab | Clicks "Run missing items" | Dialog lists the runs to be created and the trial count before and after; confirm submits a sweep |
| 2 | Sweep view | Waits or keeps working | Grid fills as members finish; each robustness item turns pass or fail |
| 3 | Robustness tab | Opens a failed item | The item's chart and a link to its comparison |
| 4 | Run analysis | Ablates or swaps weak slots; runs interaction tests | Paired runs in comparison; joint- effect heatmaps flag slots to tune together |
| 5 | Pre-launch checklist | Reaches 8 of 8 pass; reveals the hold-out once | Confirmation dialog; reveal logged with user and date; hold- out results fill in |
| 6 | Pre-launch checklist | Clicks "Promote to paper" | A paper-mode run appears in the same idea with the same analysis page |

### Flow 4: first config for a new idea

The path a new team member takes; target under 10 minutes without help.

| # | Where | User does | Screen responds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Strategy library | Clicks "New idea", names it, sets the hold-out period | The idea is created with its hold- out locked |
| 2 | Composer | Picks a registered variant per slot | Schema forms with defaults; neutral variants pre-filled where nothing is picked |
| 3 | Composer | Reviews lifecycle, timing and data snapshot | Team live settings and the latest validated snapshot pre-filled; warnings if they differ |
| 4 | Composer | Previews a date | Candidates, selected contracts and an action log explain what the config does |

## B. Page wireframes

Three wireframes fix the layout of the pages that carry most of the work. They show placement and hierarchy at desktop width (1440 px), not final styling; numbered callouts match the notes under each.

### Composer

1. Context bar: idea and config name, "Differs from baseline in 1 slot", Preview and Run; Run is the only primary button.
2. Slot board in three lifecycle columns, Idle, Armed and Open, so the card order reads like a trade's life. The open card shows its variant picker and schema form in place.
3. Open-state cards show their `open_state_order` as numbers; dragging reorders them.
4. A changed field carries a baseline dot; hover shows the baseline value and reset.

> **Diagram, page 6 of the source PDF** — *Run analysis wireframe · Overview tab, a range brushed*
>
> Not reproduced in this conversion; see `Plan/Backtesting platform UI UX design plan addendum.pdf`, page 6.

5. Settings panel: lifecycle, timing, run settings, data snapshot, book limits, collapsed to one-line summaries.
6. Bottom panel: Preview, Validation and YAML tabs; preview lists candidates and selected contracts for the chosen date.

### Run analysis

1. Context bar: idea and run breadcrumb, mode badge, Compare, Edit and rerun.
2. Realism strip, read-only, ending in the result hash; protocol flags beside it.
3. Metric cards, eight at most, each with its interval bar and baseline delta; the hero metric sits first.
4. Tabs; switching keeps range, selection and collapsed layers.
5. Chart stack on one time axis: equity with the hold-out hatched, drawdown, then the tab's own layers; the brushed range is shaded across all of them.
6. Fixed tooltip, top right of the stack, listing every layer's value at the hovered date.
7. Trade table filtered by the brush; the selected row shades its holding period above.

> **Diagram, page 7 of the source PDF** — *Trade card wireframe · drawer open over run analysis*
>
> Not reproduced in this conversion; see `Plan/Backtesting platform UI UX design plan addendum.pdf`, page 7.

8. Job tray, collapsed to a count when idle.

### Trade card

1. Sticky header: `trade_id`, underlying, dates, previous and next (J and K).
2. Conclusion: total P&L, split into main and hedge legs, with the closing slot and action.
3. Lifecycle timeline: Idle, Armed, Open, Closed, with one marker per action in its slot's color.
4. Price and P&L over the hold; stops drawn as steps; shadow tracking after exit dashed.
5. Action log; the row for the clicked marker is highlighted with its reason and triggering values.
6. Legs with role, quotes, fill and spread paid.
7. Actions: counterfactual exit, ablate this slot, open in chain explorer.

## C. Frontend architecture and data flow

A finished run never changes, so its data is cached by `run_id` forever; view state lives in the URL; only fleeting interaction state lives in a client store; and no layer derives a number the backend did not return.

Pages read view state from the URL and results from the cache; a job event from the backend invalidates only that run's entries.

### State ownership

Every piece of state has exactly one owner, which removes most sync bugs.

| State | Owner | Examples | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| View state | URL | Tab, time range, selected `trade_id`, drawer, filters, compared runs, baseline column | Shareable; back and forward work |
| Run data | Query cache, keyed by endpoint, `run_id` and params | Equity, snapshots, tradebook, metrics, attribution, events | Finished runs never expire; running jobs refetch on events |
| Interaction state | UI store | Hovered date, crosshair, brush while dragging, open menus | Current session |
| Preferences | User settings on the server | Metric card set, density, panel sizes, P&L color convention | Per user, every device |
| Drafts | Draft config on the server | Composer edits not yet submitted | Auto-saved per user |
| Job status | Event stream into the query cache | Queued, progress, finished, failed | Live |

### Loading and caching rules

1. Load in reading order: run summary and metrics, then equity and drawdown, then the active tab's layers, then the trade table. Other tabs prefetch when the user hovers them.
2. One fetch per series per page. Every chart layer reads the same cached series; brushing filters in memory and never refetches.
3. Zoom loads detail: the full period at overview resolution first, the brushed range at full resolution when zoomed. Downsampling is a drawing step only; tooltips and tables always show the exact stored values.
4. Trade tables and action logs are virtualized; sorting and filtering move to the server above 5,000 rows.
5. Job progress arrives by server-sent events (polling as fallback). A "finished" event invalidates that run's queries and raises the toast.
6. Optimistic updates only for metadata: labels, notes, archive. Results are never shown before the backend returns them.
7. Failures stay local: a layer that fails shows its own error and retry while the rest of the page renders.

### Performance budget

| Interaction | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Crosshair and hover across the whole chart stack | One frame, under 16 ms |
| Brush release to every layer and the table updated | < 100 ms |
| Tab switch with cached data | < 100 ms |
| Open a trade card | < 150 ms cached, < 500 ms uncached |
| Revisit a finished run | First paint < 1 s |
| Analysis interactive once results are ready | < 2 s for 5 years and 1,000 trades |
| Composer field validation | < 50 ms |
| Preview | ≤ 10 s |
| Initial JavaScript | < 300 KB gzipped; chart libraries loaded per tab |

### Interaction feel

- Every click is acknowledged within 100 ms: a pressed state, a skeleton or a queued row in the job tray.
- Motion only for changes of place: drawer, panel, tab underline, 150 to 200 ms. Data never animates.
- No layout shift: skeletons reserve the final size and numbers use tabular figures, so values do not jitter as they load.
- Closing the drawer returns focus and scroll to where the user was.
- Long work is a job, never a frozen page: preview, runs and sweeps all run in the background.
- Reversible metadata changes (archive, label) offer Undo in a toast instead of a confirm dialog; confirm dialogs are kept for the irreversible, such as revealing the hold-out.

### Recommended stack

| Concern | Recommendation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framework | React with TypeScript | Typed end to end against the API contract |
| Routing and URL state | TanStack Router with typed search params | The URL is typed state, not strings |
| Server data | TanStack Query | Keyed caching, invalidation, prefetch on hover |
| UI state | Zustand with selectors | Hover and crosshair updates do not re-render the page |
| Time-series stack | uPlot | Built for large time series with synced cursors across charts |
| Other charts | visx or ECharts for heatmaps, waterfalls, Gantt and surfaces | Custom marks in slot and Greek colors |
| Tables | TanStack Table with TanStack Virtual | Headless and virtualized |
| Forms from ParamSchema | JSON Schema exported from the pydantic models, rendered by one form component | One source of truth for validation and forms |
| YAML view | Monaco with a YAML language server fed the config JSON | Errors pinned to lines as the user types |

## D. Content and formatting rules

One format per kind of value, one word per concept, everywhere: researchers compare numbers across pages and runs, and a value written two ways reads as two values.

### Numbers

| Value | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Money (P&L, premium, fees) | Dollar sign, thousands separators, sign always shown; whole dollars at $1,000 and above, cents below | +$12,480 · −$3.15 |
| Option prices and fills | Two decimals, as quoted | 4.35 |
| Returns and rates | Percent with one decimal; two below 1% | 18.4% · 0.35% |
| Ratios (Sortino, Sharpe, Deflated Sharpe, payoff) | Two decimals | 1.32 |
| Intervals | Value, then the range in brackets | 1.32 [0.84, 1.77] |
| Contract Greeks | Delta and gamma two decimals; vega and theta in dollars per contract | Δ 0.42 · Θ −$0.08 / day |
| Book Greeks | Dollar terms with the unit named | Vega $1,240 per vol point · Theta −$310 per day |
| Implied volatility | Percent with one decimal; IV rank as a 0 to 100 percentile without % | IV 24.6% · IV rank 72 |
| Costs and slippage | Basis points | 3.5 bp |
| Counts | Thousands separators | 1,046 trades |
| Missing values | Empty cell, reason on hover | — |

Negatives use the true minus sign (−) plus color; units go in column headers ("P&L ($)"), not in every cell; numbers are right-aligned in tabular figures.

### Dates and time

- Market times are US Eastern and say so, on a 24-hour clock: 15:45 ET.
- Tables, ids and URLs use ISO dates (2026-10-07); prose and tooltips use Oct 7, 2026; chart axes use Oct 7.
- Expiries show the date and days to expiry together: 2026-11-20 · 44 DTE.

- Day counts state their convention in the header, trading or calendar, matching the backend's single time convention.
- Relative times ("3 min ago") only for job events, with the absolute time on hover.

### Identifiers

| Object | Shown as | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run | First 7 characters of `run_id`, monospace; full id on hover and copy | a1f3c9e |
| Trade | `trade_id` as returned, monospace | T-0132 |
| Contract | Readable form, OCC symbol on hover and copy | SPY 2026-11-20 580 C |
| Variant | Name and version | trend_breakout v1.3 |
| Data snapshot | Snapshot ID, monospace | ds-2026-09-21 |

### Terms

The interface uses the architecture's vocabulary, so screens, logs, configs and the API say the same thing.

| Use | Not | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slot | Module, component | The position in the strategy (Setup / Regime, Entry, …) |
| Variant | Plugin, implementation | What fills a slot, with a version |
| Run | Backtest result | "Job" only for queue status |
| Idea | Project, experiment | The group that owns the trial count and hold-out |
| Trade | Position | A position is a holding in accounting; a trade is a `trade_id` |
| Closing slot and action | Exit reason | E.g. "Stop Loss · CLOSE" |
| Realism assumption | Parameter | λ, latency, participation cap, mark method |
| Hold-out | Test set | Locked per idea, revealed once |
| Paper, live | Simulated, real | Run modes |

### Microcopy

- Buttons say verb and object: Run, Compare with baseline, Ablate Stop Loss, Reveal hold-out. Never OK or Submit.
- Errors say what happened and what to do next: "Preview failed: snapshot ds-2026-09- 21 has no quotes on 2024-08-05. Pick another date or snapshot."
- Warnings name the number: "Only 38 trades; conclusions need at least 60." (the minimum is a team setting)
- Confirm dialogs state the consequence: "Reveal the hold-out for this idea? This can be done once and is logged."
- Empty states say what will appear and offer one action.
- Sentence case everywhere; no exclamation marks; no "please".
